contexts.text: (Jacob) put sackcloth upon his loins () = mourning for good destroyed. Explained, Illustrated.
As to put on sackcloth, and roll themselves in ashes, represented mourning over evils and falsities, they represented also humiliation, and likewise repentance. Explained.
The Spirits who instruct... appear as if clothed in sackcloth.
The sun became black as sackcloth of hair () = all the good of love adulterated. (Explained.)

Clothed in sackcloth () = mourning on account of the non-reception of truth. By to be clothed with sackcloth, is signified mourning on account of truth being devastated in the Church; for garments = truths; and therefore to be clothed in sackcloth, which is not a garment, = mourning that there is no truth; and, where there is no truth, there is no Church, (Explained.)
That mourning on account of truth being devastated in the Church, was represented by putting on sackcloth. Illustrated.
To put off the sackcloth from off the loins () = to reveal filthy loves. Explained.
The affection of truth (lamented for) is signified by sackcloth.
Clothed in sackcloth = in mourning on account of the non-reception of Divine good and Divine truth. (Explained.)

Their rending the garments and putting on sackcloth, signified mourning on account of the desolation of truth and good in the Church, and on account of the non-reception of them... The putting on of sackcloth, signified mourning on account of the deprivation of good and truth, and the consequent vastation of the Church. Illustrated.
